answer: Because the mirror index resolves every citation against the jetty checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the hollow audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 197 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 197 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
